comments.comment: +1 on master branch: https://testing.whamcloud.com/test_sets/8bbdbfa8-bbda-4603-837b-e896396b0f38
scherementsev could you please a look at this?  I think the LQA code changed the quota functionality most recently.

adilger , unfortunately, the test was waiting too long and there is no logs that scope the period of deleting the lqe. At first look it doesn't relate to LQA. If it reproducible, we can try to decrease the timeout in sanity-quota_48 to get required period.

"Sergey Cheremencev <scherementsev@ddn.com>" uploaded a new patch: https://review.whamcloud.com/c/fs/lustre-release/+/67338
Subject: LU-20230 tests: debug changes sanity-quota 48
Project: fs/lustre-release
Branch: master
Current Patch Set: 1
Commit: 1f82f5832ad6e88d766c373f567aebb2b297c7bf

I reproduced it with 20 seconds delay in https://testing.whamcloud.com/test_sets/3c7fe3f9-5a2b-4c04-a073-a2998cb3ecbd.

It's clear why it fails. After qmt_delete_qid had finished, OST0002 got blocking_ast that caused qsd_adjust->qsd_calc_adjust. As OST0002 granted space was not zero, it sent release request to the QMT.

QMT had already removed record for project:10000 when got release request from the OST0002. However, it created a new one during release request.

According to the test session output, the previous sanity-quota_48 did IO to the file(project:10000) at the OST0002.

I'm not sure why it gets blocking_ast, but my guess is that it is because of buffered IO from the previous test case.

I'm thinking about a fix. I suppose we could start reintegration in the beginning of the sanity-quota_48.

However, there could a problem in the qsd code. From the logs it is seen that lqe at the OST0002 is enforced even after deleting:
